title: Audit log ingest & storage playbook: compact indexing, partition tiers, and cost controls
creator: Ananya Patel
description: Define and implement a production-ready playbook for ingesting, indexing, partitioning, and retaining audit logs (RBAC v2 events, SSO/SAML auth flows, admin actions). Goals: keep storage costs predictable, ensure fast queryability for recent events, and meet compliance retention rules (per-tenant and global). Deliverables: ingestion pipeline schema and throttling rules, index/partition naming and rollup TTLs, cold-storage export process, deletion/retention automation, and monitoring/runbooks for cost/regression. This ticket focuses on operational patterns and automation rather than the UI for viewing logs.
acceptance_criteria: Documented ingest schema and shard/partitioning strategy for high-volume orgs (>=10k events/min)
Implementation plan to roll daily->monthly index rollover with automated rollup for tokens and request bodies
Cost-control knobs defined: per-tenant TTL overrides, index compression, cold-export to S3 Glacier with lifecycle policy
Automated retention worker spec with safe-delete workflow and audit trail for deletion actions
Playbook includes integration notes for RBAC v2 event canonicalization and SSO/SAML assertion anonymization rules
tasks: Draft canonical audit event schema (fields, normalized actors, metadata tags)
Prototype partition key: org_id + event_date (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM depending on volume)
Define hot/warm/cold tiers and TTLs (default: hot 30d, warm 90d, cold 365d) and compression settings
Build export job to snapshot rolled indices to S3 and invoke lifecycle for Glacier transition
Add metric hooks: ingest rate, index growth GB/day, cost by org, retention exceptions
Write deletion worker with two-stage approval (scheduled mark -> delete after 7 days) and immutable deletion log
Coordinate with RBAC v2 team to include resource identifiers and policy version in events
Prepare runbook for on-call (what to check when index growth spikes)
